body.body:
## What

Link onevcs 0.52.0 and onevcs-testing 0.19.4 for repository-declared idle maintenance. Show reclaimed GiB and slot counts in `results`, with repository totals largest first, and surface unreadable declarations. Slots that grew or lack disk measurements contribute no reclaimed space.

Add six maintenance journeys and an isolated 20-identity, 25-slot workload with an 8-second overhead budget, checked during the release sweep. Update the maintenance contract notes and linked-version documentation.

## Why

Repository-declared cleanup must reach every host running the engine to reclaim accumulated output—about 926 GB on this host. Showing reclaimed space and unreadable declarations lets managers see whether cleanup is working before the disk fills.

## What

Adopt onetaskgraph 0.7.1 so documents copied from private drafts are filed under the public board’s copied plan without recording a private origin. Add an integration regression test and move judged lint to gpt-6.1-sol, preserving its fallback settings.

## Why

Plans must be drafted privately to keep private repository names out of public stores. Missing origin metadata previously prevented their documents from reaching public boards, blocking plan approval and launch. This adoption restores that workflow while preserving the privacy boundary.

body.body:
## What

Declare idle warm-pool maintenance using `cargo-prune-superseded` 0.1.1, installed by bootstrap, to remove superseded Cargo builds while retaining each unit’s newest build and everything modified within two days. Add a 20-second steady-state maintenance budget, checked after the release-PR gate and excluded from per-change checks, with coverage for installation, measurement, and task selection.

Also update locked `rustls` to 0.23.46 and fix a race in the release-wait integration test’s queue reads.

## Why

Superseded build output across the host’s pool reached roughly 926 GB and nearly filled a 1.8 TB disk twice in four days. Repository-owned cleanup keeps builds warm while reclaiming space; the budget limits how long a regular maintenance pass holds a slot out of service.

body.body:
## What

Remove dispatch scratch when a run reaches `SETTLED`; retain it at other endings and pauses, with recorded sizes and removal failures shown in `status` and `results`. Add `onepipeline scratch discard <run-id>` and its public library equivalent, preserving journals, reports and launch records.

## Why

Run directories are retained indefinitely, so dispatch scratch accumulated indefinitely too: 284 GB across 465 runs on this host, nearly filling the disk twice in four days. Successful runs can release that space, while unsuccessful or paused runs keep material needed for inspection or retry. Visible sizes and an explicit discard command make the remaining usage manageable.

## Additional info

This breaks the previous scratch-lifetime guarantee. Runs that ended before this release are not cleaned automatically; use `scratch discard` to clear their backlog. The verb refuses live or non-ended runs, including paused and host-shutdown runs. Removal never follows symlinks inside scratch, and a symlink scratch root is refused.
